aggressive_definition: High-grade prostate cancer; supplied full-text evidence identifies high grade as Gleason score 7 or higher.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Among the total 10,920 men in this analysis, 2,129 (19.5%) men were diagnosed with prostate cancer (1,425 (66.9%) Gleason score 2-6; 564 (26.5%) Gleason score 7 or higher; and 140 (6.5%) Gleason score unknown).
study_design: Prospective cohort analysis within the randomized, placebo-controlled Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial.
reason: The abstract explicitly analyzes incident total, low-grade, and high-grade prostate cancer detected during the 7-year trial. Thus it supports both general and aggressive incidence. The abstract gives 2,129 total cases, while supplied full-text evidence gives 564 Gleason score 7-or-higher cases. The total analytic N is not stated directly in the abstract and was not inferred by adding cases and cancer-free participants.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In combined arms, heavy alcohol consumption (> or =50 g of alcohol daily) and regular heavy drinking (> or =4 drinks daily on > or =5 days per week) were associated with increased risks of high-grade prostate cancer (RR, 2.01 [95% CI, 1.33-3.05] and 2.17 [95% CI, 1.42-3.30], respectively); less heavy drinking was not associated with risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row's RR of 2.01 (95% CI 1.33-3.05) is explicitly reported for high-grade prostate cancer and heavy alcohol consumption.
